subject.title: exec private-LAN access fails while same user GUI/LaunchAgent succeeds

question: Should this issue be resolved by a diagnostic-only exec warning, or should OpenClaw change gateway-host exec private-LAN reachability semantics?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing diagnostic, but allowing, denying, or detaching private-LAN exec traffic changes a security boundary and needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Land Diagnostic Only
options.body: Review and land the open diagnostic PR while keeping actual private-network access policy under the related security trackers.

options.title: Design Access Parity
options.body: Treat same-user GUI/LaunchAgent reachability as the product goal and require a separate security design before implementation.

options.title: Defer To Broader Trackers
options.body: Reject the diagnostic-only scope and keep this behavior under the broader private-network policy issues.

recommendation.title: Land Diagnostic Only
recommendation.body: Review and land the open diagnostic PR while keeping actual private-network access policy under the related security trackers.

likelyOwner.reason: The exec outcome and host-routing history most consistently points to steipete for the code path and policy-facing docs involved in this choice.
